sorters.name: Always or This Time?
sorters.blurb: Tap "Always true" for a fact, habit or rule, or "One future time" for a single possible event still to come.

items.t: If I drink milk tea after six, I can't sleep.
items.note: A habit: it happens every time, so there is no will.

items.t: Mum will be upset if I forget her birthday this Friday.
items.note: Cue: this Friday. One future day; will sits in the result half.

items.t: Plants die if they don't get any water.
items.note: A general truth about all plants: present plus present.

items.t: We won't go to the market this evening if it's still raining at five.
items.note: Cues: this evening, at five. One decision about one evening.

items.t: If I finish my homework tonight, I'll watch one episode.
items.note: Cue: tonight. One evening, one plan: if plus present, then will.

items.t: If the parcel arrives this afternoon, I'll text you a photo.
items.note: Cue: this afternoon. One possible event, one promise.

items.t: My phone gets hot if I play games for too long.
items.note: It happens whenever she plays too long: a general fact about the phone.

items.t: If it rains in Bangkok, the traffic always gets worse.
items.note: Cue: always. A general truth about the city.

items.t: If you miss the 7.15 train tomorrow, you'll be late for the test.
items.note: Cue: tomorrow. A warning about one morning.

items.t: If the BTS is crowded, I usually wait for the next train.
items.note: Cue: usually. This is what she does every time.

items.t: If you leave ice cream in the sun, it melts in minutes.
items.note: A fact that is true every time: present plus present.

items.t: If Ploy comes to the concert on Saturday, I'll save her a seat.
items.note: Cue: on Saturday. A promise about one event.

items.t: I'll lend you my notes tonight if you promise to return them by Monday.
items.note: Cues: tonight, by Monday. A deal about one occasion.

items.t: If students arrive after eight, they sign the late book.
items.note: A school rule: it is the same every day.

items.t: If it rains tomorrow, we'll play badminton indoors.
items.note: Cue: tomorrow. One possible future event, so the result takes will.

items.t: You can borrow three books at a time if you have a library card.
items.note: A library rule, true on any day: can gives the permission.

items.t: If my cat hears the fridge open, she always runs to the kitchen.
items.note: Cue: always. A habit, so present plus present.

items.t: If Mum cooks green curry, the whole flat always smells wonderful.
items.note: Cue: always. It happens every time she cooks it.

items.t: If the haze is bad tomorrow morning, sports day might be postponed.
items.note: Cue: tomorrow morning. One day; might shows the result is only possible.

items.t: If you mix blue and yellow, you get green.
items.note: True every time you do it: a fact, not a prediction.

items.t: If you see Fah at lunch today, tell her about the room change.
items.note: Cue: today. One future moment; the result is an instruction for that moment.

items.t: If Nan passes Friday's maths quiz, she'll celebrate with mango sticky rice.
items.note: Cue: Friday's quiz. One event still to come.

items.t: If you don't charge your phone now, it'll die before we get home.
items.note: Cues: now, before we get home. A warning about this one journey.

items.t: Water boils if you heat it to 100 degrees.
items.note: A science fact. The if half can come second: the meaning is the same.

items.t: If you heat ice, it melts.
items.note: A science fact: present in both halves, true every time.

items.t: If there are still tickets at ten tomorrow, I'll buy two.
items.note: Cue: at ten tomorrow. One sale, one plan.

items.t: If the fire alarm rings, always walk to the field.
items.note: Cue: always. A standing rule: the result is an instruction for every time.

items.t: If we win the match on Sunday, Coach will buy us all bubble tea.
items.note: Cue: on Sunday. One match that has not been played yet.

sorters.name: Real or Imagined?
sorters.blurb: Tap "Real" if nothing is denied, "Imagined now" if it is not true now, or "Imagined past" if it did not happen.

items.t: If I had left earlier this morning, I'd have caught the train.
items.note: Two steps back: had left, would have caught. Truth: I left late and missed it.

items.t: If we leave at seven tomorrow, we might catch the first train.
items.note: Real future: it is still possible. Might means maybe.

items.t: If I didn't have a test tomorrow, I'd come with you tonight.
items.note: Didn't have is a past form, but not past time. Truth: I have a test tomorrow.

items.t: If we lived near the BTS, I'd sleep until seven.
items.note: Lived is a past form about now. Truth: we don't live near the BTS.

items.t: If you heat chocolate, it melts.
items.note: Real, always: a fact. Nothing is denied, so there is no Truth line.

items.t: I'd buy those headphones today if I had enough pocket money.
items.note: Cue: today. Truth: I don't have enough pocket money.

items.t: You can join the trip next week if your mum signs the form.
items.note: Real future: she may sign it. Can gives the permission.

items.t: If I were taller, I could reach the top shelf.
items.note: Were and could are one step back. Truth: I'm not tall enough to reach it.

items.t: If you're cold, close the window.
items.note: Real now: maybe you are cold. The result is an instruction.

items.t: If we had bought tickets last week, we'd have got front-row seats.
items.note: Cue: last week. Truth: we didn't buy them then.

items.t: Last term, if the teacher was late, we always started reading quietly.
items.note: Real past habit: it happened. Past plus past is not imagined here.

items.t: If you had told me on Monday, I might have helped you.
items.note: Cue: on Monday, with had told and might have. Truth: you didn't tell me then.

items.t: If my phone had more memory, I could keep all these photos.
items.note: One step back: had, could. Truth: it doesn't have enough memory.

items.t: If Praew were here now, she'd fix this in a minute.
items.note: Cue: now. Truth: Praew isn't here.

items.t: If it rains tomorrow, we'll take a taxi.
items.note: Real future: present after if, will in the result. It may really rain.

items.t: If Fah was at practice yesterday, she already knows the new plan.
items.note: Real past: maybe she was there. Nothing is denied, and there is no would.

items.t: If Bam had saved her file, she wouldn't have lost her essay last night.
items.note: Cue: last night. Truth: she didn't save it and she lost the essay.

items.t: I wouldn't have got wet yesterday if I'd taken my umbrella.
items.note: Here 'd is had, and would have is the past ticket. Truth: I didn't take it and I got wet.

items.t: If I had a cat, I'd call her Mochi.
items.note: One step back: had, would. Truth: I don't have a cat now.

items.t: We'd have won last Sunday's match if Jane hadn't hurt her ankle.
items.note: Cue: last Sunday. Truth: she hurt her ankle and we lost.

items.t: If Fern had seen the message, she'd have come to practice on Friday.
items.note: Cue: on Friday. Truth: she didn't see it, so she didn't come.

items.t: If Mint calls tonight, tell her I'm at badminton.
items.note: Real future: she may call. Present after if, then an instruction.

items.t: If the cat hadn't knocked my glass over, my notes would have stayed dry.
items.note: Had plus V3, would have plus V3. Truth: she knocked it over and the notes got wet.

items.t: If it weren't raining now, we'd be on the court.
items.note: Cue: now. Truth: it is raining, so we aren't on the court.

items.t: If I knew the answer, I'd tell you right now.
items.note: Cue: right now. Truth: I don't know the answer.

items.t: In primary school, if it rained at break, we played in the hall.
items.note: Real past: it really happened, many times. Past plus past, and no would.

items.t: If my cat is hungry, she sits on my keyboard.
items.note: Real, always: a habit. Present plus present.

items.t: If it hadn't rained yesterday, we would have had sports day.
items.note: Cue: yesterday, with had and would have. Truth: it rained, so there was no sports day.

items.t: If Nan had charged her phone last night, she could have called us.
items.note: Cue: last night. Truth: she didn't charge it, so she couldn't call.

items.t: If I spoke Korean, I might understand this song without subtitles.
items.note: Spoke is one step back from speak. Truth: I don't speak Korean.

sorters.name: Glitch Hunt
sorters.blurb: Tap "Clean" if the sentence is correct, or "Glitched" if it has a grammar error.

items.t: If I would have more time now, I would learn Korean.
items.note: Would in the if half. Fix: If I had more time now, I would learn Korean.

items.t: I wish I can come to your party tonight, but I have tutoring.
items.note: Wish plus present. Fix: I wish I could come to your party tonight, but I have tutoring.

items.t: We'll be late unless we don't leave now.
items.note: Unless plus not. Fix: We'll be late unless we leave now.

items.t: If you'll follow me, I'll show you to your seats.
items.note: Clean, and it only looks odd: here will means are willing to. It is a polite request.

items.t: Unless you don't hurry, you'll miss the bus.
items.note: Unless already means if not. Fix: Unless you hurry, you'll miss the bus.

items.t: If I will see Mint tomorrow, I'll give her your book.
items.note: Will after if. Fix: If I see Mint tomorrow, I'll give her your book.

items.t: Take an umbrella in case it rains this afternoon.
items.note: Clean: you take it now, before any rain. That is a precaution.

items.t: If Nan had studied, she would pass last Friday's quiz.
items.note: No past ticket. Fix: If Nan had studied, she would have passed last Friday's quiz.

items.t: If it rains on Saturday, we'll watch a film at home.
items.note: Clean: present after if, will only in the result.

items.t: If it hadn't rained, we would have went to the market.
items.note: Wrong verb form after have. Fix: If it hadn't rained, we would have gone to the market.

items.t: If Ploy had seen the message, she might have come on Friday.
items.note: Clean: might have plus V3 is a possible past result. Truth: she didn't see it.

items.t: If I am you, I would tell the teacher today.
items.note: Present for an imagined present. Fix: If I were you, I would tell the teacher today.

items.t: If she has seen your message yesterday, she would have replied.
items.note: Has seen should be had seen. Fix: If she had seen your message yesterday, she would have replied.

items.t: If I had left earlier, I would catch the 7.15 train yesterday.
items.note: No past ticket. Fix: If I had left earlier, I would have caught the 7.15 train yesterday.

items.t: If I were you, I'd say sorry to her this afternoon.
items.note: Clean: were and would are one step back. Truth: I'm not you.

items.t: In case it rains tomorrow, we'll cancel the picnic.
items.note: In exam English, in case is only for a precaution you take before the event. Cancelling is a result. Fix: If it rains tomorrow, we'll cancel the picnic.

items.t: I wish I had brought my umbrella this morning.
items.note: Clean: wish plus had plus V3 for a past regret. Truth: I didn't bring it.

items.t: If I had left earlier yesterday, I would have caught the train.
items.note: Clean: had plus V3, would have plus V3. Truth: I left late and missed it.

items.t: If you heat butter, it melts.
items.note: Clean: a fact, present plus present.

items.t: If I would have known about the quiz, I would have studied.
items.note: Would in the if half: heard in American speech, wrong in exams. Fix: If I had known about the quiz, I would have studied.

items.t: If I have known about the traffic, I would have taken the BTS.
items.note: Have known should be had known. Fix: If I had known about the traffic, I would have taken the BTS.

items.t: You can borrow my charger as long as you give it back tonight.
items.note: Clean: as long as sets the condition for the deal.

items.t: When we were little, if it rained, we stayed in and played cards.
items.note: Clean, and it only looks odd: a real past habit takes past plus past, with no would.

items.t: If I'd had my card, I would have took the BTS.
items.note: Wrong verb form after have. Fix: If I'd had my card, I would have taken the BTS.

items.t: I wish I had a cat, but Mum is allergic.
items.note: Clean: wish plus past for a wish about now. Truth: I don't have a cat.

items.t: If I have wings, I would fly to school every day.
items.note: Present for an imagined present. Fix: If I had wings, I would fly to school every day.

items.t: We would have gone to the market if it hadn't rained on Sunday.
items.note: Clean: would have plus V3 (gone). Truth: it rained, so we didn't go.

items.t: If we hadn't missed the BTS, we wouldn't be late now.
items.note: Clean: a past condition with a result now. Truth: we missed it, and we are late.

items.t: If I was rude this morning, I'm sorry.
items.note: Clean, and it only looks odd: a real past possibility. Maybe I was rude, so was is right.

items.t: I'll buy the tickets in case I have enough money.
items.note: In case is only for a precaution against a risk. Money is the condition here. Fix: I'll buy the tickets if I have enough money.

items.t: If it will rain tomorrow, we'll stay at home.
items.note: Will after if. Fix: If it rains tomorrow, we'll stay at home.

items.t: If I had more pocket money now, I could buy that sketchbook.
items.note: Clean: had and could are one step back. Truth: I don't have enough money now.

items.t: If I'd known about the quiz, I'd have studied last night.
items.note: Clean: the first 'd is had, the second is would. Truth: I didn't know.

items.t: If you see Fah at lunch, tell her I'm looking for her.
items.note: Clean: present after if, then an instruction.

items.t: I wish I have a cat, but Mum is allergic.
items.note: Wish plus present. Fix: I wish I had a cat, but Mum is allergic.

items.t: Unless you hurry, you'll miss the bus.
items.note: Clean: unless means if you don't, so no extra not.

sorters.name: Type Sorter
sorters.blurb: Tap the type of each sentence: check the time of the if half, then the time of the result half.

items.t: If it's sunny on Saturday, we might go to the park.
items.note: First: cue on Saturday. A real future; might means maybe.

items.t: I'd walk to school every day if I lived next door to it.
items.note: Second: lived, would plus verb. Truth: I don't live next door.

items.t: If we had caught the 7.15 train, we would be at school by now.
items.note: Mixed 3/2: cue by now. Truth: we missed the train; we aren't at school yet.

items.t: If Jane weren't such a calm player, she'd have lost Sunday's final.
items.note: Mixed 2/3: Jane is calm (always), so she didn't lose (Sunday).

items.t: I'd know the answer now if I had listened in yesterday's lesson.
items.note: Mixed 3/2: the result comes first. I didn't listen yesterday; I don't know now.

items.t: If we don't leave in five minutes, we'll miss the train.
items.note: First: one possible future event, with will in the result.

items.t: If I see Ploy tomorrow, I'll give her your notes.
items.note: First: cue tomorrow. Present after if, will in the result.

items.t: If I had a bigger room, I'd keep a piano in it.
items.note: Second: had, would plus verb. Truth: my room isn't big enough now.

items.t: If I were taller, I'd have reached the top shelf yesterday.
items.note: Mixed 2/3: a permanent condition, a past result. Truth: I'm not tall enough; I didn't reach it.

items.t: If you tap your card at the gate, it opens.
items.note: Zero: it works like this every time.

items.t: If Praew didn't love cats, she wouldn't have adopted three last year.
items.note: Mixed 2/3: she loves cats (always), so she adopted three (last year).

items.t: If I eat late at night, I always sleep badly.
items.note: Zero: cue always. A habit, present plus present.

items.t: I'll message you tonight if my order arrives.
items.note: First: cue tonight. Will in the result, present after if.

items.t: If it had rained on sports day, the races would have been cancelled.
items.note: Third: had rained, would have been cancelled. Truth: it didn't rain and the races went ahead.

items.t: If the haze is bad, our school always cancels outdoor PE.
items.note: Zero: cue always. A school habit, present plus present.

items.t: What would you do if you found a wallet outside 7-Eleven?
items.note: Second: found, would plus verb. An imagined situation: you haven't found one.

items.t: If Mint doesn't practise this week, she won't be ready for Friday's match.
items.note: First: a warning about one future match. Won't is will not.

items.t: If I were you, I'd say sorry to Fern today.
items.note: Second: were, would plus verb. Advice about now. Truth: I'm not you.

items.t: If I'd eaten breakfast this morning, I wouldn't be hungry now.
items.note: Mixed 3/2: had eaten this morning, would be now. Truth: I didn't eat; I am hungry.

items.t: Bam would have won last week's quiz if she had read the last question carefully.
items.note: Third: last week in both halves. Truth: she didn't read it carefully and didn't win.

items.t: If it hadn't rained all night, the court would be dry now.
items.note: Mixed 3/2: it rained in the night; the court is wet now.

items.t: If we didn't have school tomorrow, we could stay up late tonight.
items.note: Second: didn't have, could plus verb. Truth: we have school tomorrow.

items.t: If you freeze water, it turns into ice.
items.note: Zero: a fact. Present plus present, true every time.

items.t: If I had taken my umbrella yesterday, I wouldn't have got wet.
items.note: Third: both halves are about yesterday. Truth: I didn't take it and I got wet.

items.t: If the order had arrived on Friday, I could have worn the shoes to the party.
items.note: Third: had arrived, could have worn. Truth: it came too late for the party.

items.t: If my cat could talk, she would complain about dinner every day.
items.note: Second: could, would plus verb. Truth: my cat can't talk.

items.t: If you hadn't reminded me, I would have forgotten Mum's birthday last month.
items.note: Third, for relief. Truth: you reminded me, so I didn't forget.

items.t: If I knew her LINE ID, I'd add her right now.
items.note: Second: cue right now. Truth: I don't know her LINE ID.

items.t: I might have passed Monday's test if I had slept more the night before.
items.note: Third: might have passed, had slept. Both are past. Truth: I didn't sleep enough.

items.t: If I had charged my phone last night, it would still be working.
items.note: Mixed 3/2: cue still. Truth: I didn't charge it; it isn't working now.

items.t: If you don't water basil, it dies quickly.
items.note: Zero: a fact about the plant. Present plus present.

items.t: If I had slept earlier last night, I wouldn't be so tired now.
items.note: Mixed 3/2: past condition, result now. Truth: I slept late; I am tired now.

items.t: My little cousin cries if she hears thunder.
items.note: Zero: it happens every time. Present plus present.

items.t: If I spoke Japanese, I would have understood the film last night.
items.note: Mixed 2/3: spoke is about now and always, would have understood is about last night. Truth: I don't speak Japanese.

items.t: If I knew how to swim, I would have joined the pool party last weekend.
items.note: Mixed 2/3: I can't swim (now and always), so I didn't join (last weekend).

items.t: Cats purr if they feel safe.
items.note: Zero: a general truth about cats. Present plus present.

items.t: If Nan hadn't lost her card yesterday, she could be on the BTS with us now.
items.note: Mixed 3/2: lost it yesterday, isn't with us now. Could be is a result now.

items.t: If we'd left at six this morning, we'd have caught the first train.
items.note: Third: 'd left is had left, 'd have caught is would have caught. Truth: we left later and missed it.

items.t: If I weren't afraid of heights, I'd have gone on the big wheel on Saturday.
items.note: Mixed 2/3: I am afraid of heights (always), so I didn't go on it (Saturday).

items.t: If the shop is still open at nine tonight, I'll get some milk.
items.note: First: cue tonight. Present after if, will in the result.

items.t: If our flat were bigger, we could have had the party at home last month.
items.note: Mixed 2/3: the flat is small (always), so the party wasn't at home (last month).

items.t: If you help me with maths this evening, I'll buy you a bubble tea.
items.note: First: cue this evening. A deal about one future time.

sorters.name: Connector Clash
sorters.blurb: Tap the one connector that fits the gap: unless, in case, as long as or even if.

items.t: ___ we leave right now, we'll miss the train. Come on, we can still make it!
items.note: Except test: we'll miss it, except if we leave now. Cue: we can still make it.

items.t: My laptop is old, so I always save my essay twice ___ it crashes.
items.note: Umbrella test: she saves first, because a crash might come later.

items.t: Praew is a great sport: she smiles ___ she loses a match.
items.note: Losing does not change the result: she smiles either way.

items.t: Coach lets us choose the music ___ we finish the warm-up properly.
items.note: A deal with Coach: music, on one condition.

items.t: The shop will change the shoes ___ you keep your receipt.
items.note: A condition for a promise: receipt first, then the exchange.

items.t: Don't wake me before nine tomorrow ___ the parcel arrives. I need to sign for it.
items.note: Except test: don't wake me, except if the parcel comes.

items.t: A taxi won't help: we'd still be late ___ we took one now.
items.note: A taxi would not change the result: late either way. Cue: a taxi won't help.

items.t: I'll watch any film with you tonight ___ it isn't a horror film. I hate those.
items.note: Any film is fine on one condition: no horror.

items.t: I'll screenshot the ticket now ___ there's no signal at the gate later.
items.note: Umbrella test: take the screenshot now, before the possible problem.

items.t: Mum says I can't go to the concert ___ I finish my project first. So I'm finishing it!
items.note: Except test: no concert, except if the project is done. Finishing it opens the door.

items.t: Write my number on your hand ___ your phone dies at the concert.
items.note: Umbrella test: write it now, before anything goes wrong.

items.t: The cat can sleep on my bed ___ she doesn't bite my toes.
items.note: A deal with the cat. Unless would not work here: the clause already has not.

items.t: We'll get good seats ___ we arrive before the doors open.
items.note: A condition that makes the good result happen: arrive early, sit well.

items.t: Mum gave me 100 baht extra ___ I needed a taxi home.
items.note: Umbrella test in the past: the money came first, for a possible need later.

items.t: You won't improve at badminton ___ you practise, so come to training twice a week.
items.note: Except test: no progress, except if you practise.

items.t: I'm going to practice tonight ___ it pours with rain. Nothing can stop me.
items.note: The rain changes nothing: she goes either way.

items.t: The cat never comes when I call, ___ I shake the food box. That always works.
items.note: Except test: she never comes, except if I shake the box.

items.t: Mum says I can go to the concert ___ I'm home by ten.
items.note: A deal with Mum: permission, with one condition.

items.t: You can sit with us ___ you promise not to spoil the ending.
items.note: A deal: a seat, on one condition.

items.t: Sports day will be on Friday ___ the haze gets worse. In that case, it moves to Monday.
items.note: Except test: Friday, except if the haze gets worse.

items.t: My cat won't move from my chair ___ I offer her a treat. Nothing works!
items.note: The treat changes nothing. Cue: nothing works.

items.t: Let's take some snacks on the trip ___ we get hungry on the bus.
items.note: Umbrella test: pack now, because hunger might come later.

items.t: The train left five minutes early. I'd have missed it ___ I had run all the way, so I'm glad I walked.
items.note: Running would not have changed the result: missed either way. Truth: the train left early.

items.t: I'm wearing my new trainers to the match ___ they get muddy. I don't care!
items.note: Mud changes nothing: she wears them either way. Cue: I don't care.

items.t: You can borrow my charger ___ you give it back before lunch.
items.note: A deal: yes, but only on this condition.

items.t: Keep your mask on outside today ___ the sky looks clear; the haze is still there.
items.note: A clear sky changes nothing: keep the mask on either way.

items.t: I'm bringing a mask ___ the haze comes back this afternoon.
items.note: Umbrella test: she packs the mask before the haze, because it might come.

items.t: I'll walk to school tomorrow ___ it rains. Then I'll take the bus.
items.note: Except test: I'll walk, except if it rains. Rain is the one thing that changes the plan.

items.t: Take an umbrella ___ it rains this afternoon; the sky looks grey.
items.note: Umbrella test: you take it now, before any rain. A precaution.

items.t: This morning we left at six ___ the traffic was bad on the way.
items.note: Umbrella test in the past: they left early because bad traffic was possible.

items.t: No card, no entry: you can't use the library ___ you show your student card.
items.note: Except test: no entry, except if you show the card.

items.t: No excuses: I'll finish this project tonight ___ I have to stay up until midnight.
items.note: Staying up late will not change the result: the project gets finished. Cue: no excuses.

machine.base: Ploy left home late this morning and missed the 7.15 BTS train. Lessons have started, and she is still on her way to school.

1.s: If Ploy leaves home by seven, she'll catch the 7.15 train.
1.truth: Said before it happened: she can still leave on time and catch it.

2.s: If Ploy were in class now, she'd be sitting next to Fah.
2.truth: She isn't in class now: she is still on her way to school.

3.s: If Ploy had left home by seven, she would have caught the 7.15 train.
3.truth: She left home late this morning and missed the train.

m32.s: If Ploy had caught the 7.15 train, she would be in class by now.
m32.truth: She missed the train this morning, so she isn't in class now.

m23.s: If Ploy lived nearer the station, she wouldn't have missed the train this morning.
m23.truth: She lives a long way from the station, and she missed the train this morning.

wish.s: Ploy: "If only I had left home ten minutes earlier!"
wish.truth: Ploy didn't leave earlier: she left late.

machine.base: It rained all Friday morning, so sports day was cancelled. It is Friday afternoon now: the rain has stopped, but the field is too wet and the students are in their classrooms.

1.s: If it rains on Friday morning, sports day will be cancelled.
1.truth: Said before it happened: Friday could still be dry.

2.s: If the field were dry, the students would be out there racing now.
2.truth: The field isn't dry, so they are in their classrooms now.

3.s: If it hadn't rained this morning, the races would have gone ahead.
3.truth: It rained this morning, so there were no races.

m32.s: If it hadn't rained all morning, the field wouldn't be too wet to run on now.
